title: Check files with try_files
summary: try_files checks candidate paths and uses a final fallback when none exists. Static generated pages often need directory index handling.
introduction: try_files checks candidate paths and uses a final fallback when none exists. Static generated pages often need directory index handling. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: try_files checks candidate paths and uses a final fallback when none exists. Static generated pages often need directory index handling.
Nginx tries a file, then a directory. If neither exists, it returns status 404.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Trace requests for an existing CSS file and a missing page.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not rewrite every missing asset to HTML; a script request needs a script, not the home page.
For more detail later, use this [Nginx further reading](https://nginx.org/en/docs/beginners_guide.html).
